name: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Analysis
objective: Quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations regulated the dynamics and ultimate fate of established droplet cool flames using FLEX flight data
what_varied: Forcing amplitude and frequency, ambient composition, pressure, forcing modes (convection, heat flux, combined), droplet diameter (sub-millimeter to 1-4 mm)

name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (ACME CFI-G)
o2_percent: 12 - 85% (ambient 18-40% in normal flames; burner flow 12-85% in inverse flames)
sensors: cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, thermocouples
objective: Determine conditions for cool diffusion flames for gaseous fuels, normal and inverse flames, and broad range of Zst, Tad, and flow rates
what_varied: Fuels, reactant dilutions, flow rates, pressures, convection direction (normal and inverse), XO2 (0.18 - 0.40 ambient in normal flames; 0.12 - 0.85 burner flow in inverse flames)
notes: Only row with a test-by-test Moon-base match: 20 normal-flame tests at 33-39% ambient O2 and 7.35 psi (0.5 atm), 17 with hot ignition (PSI-159 experiment table). Burner flow up to 85% O2 in inverse flames.

name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design (ACME/Flame Design)
o2_percent: 19.8 - 85% (ambient 19.8-40% in normal flames; burner flow 21.2-85% in inverse flames)
sensors: cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, thermocouples
objective: Obtain soot-inception limits, temperatures, detailed measurements, and extinction limits in quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames for C2H4 and CH4
what_varied: Fuel (C2H4, CH4), flow rate, Zst, amount of inert (N2 or CO2), pressure, flame type (normal and inverse), XO2
notes: Ambient O2 reached 40% only at ~1 atm (13.7-19.1 psi); the low-pressure tests (down to 6.2 psi) were inverse flames, where the high O2 is burner flow, not the chamber atmosphere (PSI-10 experiment tables).

name: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds in Microgravity with Comparison to BASS Experiments using Two-Color Tomography
fuel_detail: polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) (flat sheets, spheres, rods), wax cylinders
sensors: DSLR cameras
objective: Develop and validate flamelet generated manifold (FGM) modeling for concurrent flame spread in microgravity using BASS/BASS-II benchmarks to predict spacecraft material flammability limits
what_varied: BASS sample geometries (flat sheets, spheres, rods, cylinders), gravity conditions (microgravity vs normal-gravity)

name: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
sensors: DSLR cameras (Nikon NEF images)
objective: Derive temperature distributions and soot volume fractions from SPICE data, improve understanding of soot formation, oxidation, and aggregate growth in heavily sooting flames, and reconcile 1g vs 0g flame behavior
what_varied: Gravity (microgravity vs normal gravity), burner configuration (Yale and ACME burners), soot evolution parameters (radiation, scattering, boundary conditions)

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight (SAME-R)
sensors: M-pass, DustTrak, ionization detector, thermal precipitators (TEM grids)
objective: Quantify the sizes that liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity and relate droplet size distribution to smoke generation and transport conditions
what_varied: Materials (Pyrell foam, Kapton), heating temperatures, flow conditions (8.1 cm/s vs no-flow), aging time

name: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
objective: Use numerical simulation to explore the influence of gravity on pyrolysis smoke growth, quantify differences between 0g and 1g smoke, and identify fluid dynamic mechanisms
what_varied: Gravity (microgravity vs Earth gravity), cross-flow velocities (two speeds), thermophoresis, particle settling
notes: Pyrolysis vapor / smoke aerosol growth simulation using DBP precursor.

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I (SAFFIRE-I)
sensors: two cameras, thermocouples, two radiometers, solid state pressure sensors, CO2 and O2 sensors, two anemometers
objective: Determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and investigate low-g flammability limits compared to normal gravity screening tests
what_varied: Flow direction (Concurrent vs Opposed), burn time (420 s vs 70 s)
what_same: SIBAL fabric, dimensions (94 x 40.6 x 0.37 cm), airflow (20 cm/s), ignition power (182 W), ignition time (8 s), oxygen percent (21.5-21.7%)

name: Cool Flames Investigation (CFI)
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
sensors: black-and-white camera, UV camera, narrow-band and wide-band radiometers, high resolution cameras
objective: Examine combustion behavior of n-dodecane and mixtures at 0.25 to 5 atm, analyze helium dilution effects, and investigate relationship between droplet size, pressure, and flame extinction
what_varied: Pressure (0.5 to 5 atm flown; objective states 0.25 to 5 atm), inert diluents (nitrogen, helium), fuels (n-dodecane, farnesane, mixtures), fiber tethering (free vs SiC fiber)

name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / Far Field Box
sensors: two smoke detectors, video cameras, thermophoretic soot samplers (TEM probes)
objective: Quantify the sizes that liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity, relate droplet size distribution to smoke generation and transport conditions, and develop numerical growth models
what_varied: Sample materials (Teflon, Kapton, silicone), air flow (5 vs 10 cm/s), weight loss rate (1 vs 2 mg/min), aging duration (1 to 20 minutes)

name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE)
sensors: high resolution camera, flow rate sensors, temperature sensors
objective: Understand structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity, determine liftoff velocity limits for different fuels and burner diameters, and evaluate nitrogen dilution impact on soot and stability
what_varied: Fuels (CH4, C2H4), fuel dilution with nitrogen (20% to 100%), burner diameters, coflow velocity

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II (SAFFIRE-II)
fuel_detail: SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass), silicone, PMMA (structured and flat), PMMA with Nomex
sensors: two cameras, thermocouples, two radiometers, solid state pressure sensors, CO2 and O2 sensors, two anemometers
objective: Determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and investigate low-g flammability limits compared to normal gravity material screening tests
what_varied: Sample materials (SIBAL, silicone, PMMA, PMMA with Nomex), sample thickness (0.27 to 1.03 mm), air flow (20 or 30 cm/s), flow direction (concurrent vs opposed)
what_same: Sample dimensions (5 cm x 29 cm), ignition power (80 W), ignition time (9.2 s), Cygnus flow duct

name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment (SPICE)
fuel_detail: methane, ethylene, propane, propylene, propylene mixtures
sensors: still and video cameras, co-flow air velocity sensors, radiometers
objective: Identify laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames under various co-flow conditions in microgravity, determine effects of burner diameter and co-flow velocity, and quantify sooting propensity
what_varied: Fuels (methane, ethylene, propane, propylene), burner diameter (0.41 to 1.6 mm), co-flow velocity (5.4 to 65 cm/s), fuel flow rates (51 to 138 sccm)

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III (SAFFIRE-III)
sensors: two cameras, thermocouples, two radiometers, solid state pressure sensors, CO2 and O2 sensors, two anemometers
objective: Determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and investigate low-g flammability limits compared to normal gravity screening tests
what_varied: Flow direction (Concurrent vs Opposed)
what_same: SIBAL Fabric, dimensions (.33 x 94 x 40.6 cm), air flow (30 cm/s), Cygnus flow duct

name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME CLD Flame)
sensors: cameras (OH* and CH* chemiluminescence, color digital camera), laser extinction, thin-filament pyrometry, S-type thermocouples
objective: Characterize behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene as function of velocity and dilution (shape, lift-off, temperatures, extinction limits) and sooting tendencies
what_varied: Fuels (methane, ethylene), fuel dilution with nitrogen (25% to 40% CH4), velocity, mass flow rates

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II)
fuel_detail: PMMA (100, 200, 300 micron films, rods, slabs, spheres), cellulose, composite fabric
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / small wind tunnel
sensors: video cameras, radiometers, CSA-CP and CDM sensors, CO and CO2 sensors
objective: Study ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity to improve fire safety and suppression
what_varied: Forced flow velocity (speed up to 40 cm/s, direction: concurrent vs opposed), oxygen concentration (N2 vitiation), sample geometry (films, rods, slabs, spheres)

name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator (ACME BRE)
hardware: ACME / Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) (25 and 50 mm circular burners)
sensors: heat flux sensor, burner surface temperature sensor
objective: Establish burning conditions in quiescent microgravity for CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2 on porous circular burners at various pressures and O2 concentrations to emulate condensed fuel burning
what_varied: Fuel mixture (100% C2H4, 50% C2H4, CH4), burner diameter (25 and 50 mm), oxygen concentration (21% to 40%), pressure (8.2 to 14.7 psia), fuel flow rate
what_same: quiescent ambient (no air flow), microgravity, circular burner geometry
notes: PSI-20 objectives list planned exploration atmospheres 14.7 psia/21% O2, 10.2 psia/26.5% and 8.2 psia/34%. The flight log lists O2 (21-40%) by test day but says chamber pressures 'are not identified in this summary table', so per-test pairing is unconfirmed.

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2)
fuel_detail: iso-octane, n-octane, heptane, decane, ethanol (pure and mixtures)
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
sensors: high speed color camera video, chamber pressure and temperature sensors
objective: Provide benchmark data on bi-component droplet combustion, study liquid-phase mixing, steady/unsteady combustion, soot formation, and flame extinction mechanisms
what_varied: Fuel type, ambient gas composition (O2/N2, O2/He), oxygen mole fraction (0.17 to 0.30 per experiment table; 0.1 to 0.4 per approach text), pressure (0.5 to 3.0 atm), droplet diameter (1.5 to 5 mm), translation velocity (0.1 to 5 cm/s)
what_same: microgravity, CIR/MDCA apparatus, ambient temperature (25 C)
notes: Experiment table lists O2 options (0.17-0.30) and pressure options (0.5-3.0 atm) per fuel, not per test, so it cannot confirm 30% O2 and 0.5 atm in the same burn.

name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME E-FIELD Flames)
sensors: high-resolution cameras, spectral imaging, thermopile detectors, ion current sensors
objective: Understand relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze dynamic flame response, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames
what_varied: Electric field strength up to 10 kV (mimicked partial gravity by acting on flame ions), mesh polarity, fuel type (CH4, C2H4), fuel dilution with N2 (40% to 100%), fuel flow rate, coflow velocity
notes: Electric field acted on flame ions to mimic partial gravity; only partial-gravity-related investigation in dataset.

name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME s-Flame)
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / ACME (spherical porous burner)
sensors: spectrally resolved imaging, flame and burner thermocouples, radiative flux radiometers
objective: Measure transient structure of spherical diffusion flames, determine convective and radiative extinction limits for H2/CH4 and C2H4, and determine pulsating instabilities
what_varied: Fuels (H2, CH4, C2H4), fuel dilution with N2/He/CO2 (45% CH4, 50% C2H4, 100% H2), oxygen concentration (~21% to 30%), reactant flow rates
notes: ~30% O2 tests ran at ~1 atm; pressure rises and O2 drops with vitiation (PSI-23 experiment table), so not a Moon-base pressure match.

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
fuel_detail: methanol, n-heptane, n-octane, n-decane, n-butanol, Jet-A
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
sensors: high-resolution cameras, heat radiation radiometers, temperature sensors
objective: Map flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity, measure effectiveness of gaseous fire suppressants (CO2, He, SF6), and determine Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI)
what_varied: Fuels (methanol, alkanes), droplet size (~1.6 to 3 mm), ambient oxygen mole fraction, suppressants (CO2, He, SF6), pressure (0.69 to 3.05 atm flown; 0.5 to 1.5 atm planned for LOI tests)
notes: 17 tests at 30-34% O2 ran at 10.3-10.5 psi, just above the 10.2 psi Moon-base cutoff (PSI-69 experiment table).

name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test / Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test-2 (DAFT / DAFT-2)
fuel_detail: no fuel burned (dust aerosol test), Arizona Road Dust (ARD Fine), isopropanol
sensors: modified TSI P-Trak particulate counter, DustTrak CNC
objective: Demonstrate functionality of modified TSI P-Trak in microgravity, compare against DustTrak control, and create aerosol standards to mitigate risk for SAME fire detection
what_varied: Instrumentation (modified P-Trak vs DustTrak), sampling locations (Express rack 4, Port rack 6, Node 1)
what_same: microgravity, aerosol standard (ARD with GN2), 15-liter Mylar bags
notes: Particle counter verification in microgravity; no fuel burned.

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
fuel_detail: SIBAL (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass), Nomex fabric, Ultem, PMMA spheres
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / flow duct (76 mm x 76 mm)
sensors: cameras (top and edge profile flame imaging)
objective: Bridge the gap between normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test #1, ground tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity, and assess gaseous extinguishing agent (nitrogen) effectiveness
what_varied: Materials (SIBAL, Nomex, Ultem, PMMA), geometries (fabric, spheres, cylinders), airflow speeds (up to 40 cm/s), flow direction (concurrent vs opposed)
what_same: microgravity, MSG flow duct (76 mm x 76 mm)

name: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames
hardware: Principal Investigator Laboratory Hardware / counterflow burner
sensors: CH2O PLIF, thermometry
objective: Develop diagram of flammability limits of diffusional cool flames using FLEX data, bridge gap between flammability and extinction limits of hot/cool flames, and obtain quantitative extinction data
what_varied: Oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure (up to 20 atm), fuels (DME, n-heptane, methane), ozone sensitization (with vs without ozone)
notes: Ground-based laboratory counterflow flames at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm); low relevance to spacecraft habitat conditions.
